persona: quickstart: Python developer who just cloned the repo; goal = zero to a working run of the shipped example, then understand the outputs (Windows 11, Git Bash + PowerShell, fake provider / param_lhs only)
journey: Abbreviations used below: S = $S, V = S\venv\Scripts\python.exe (fresh venv). Started reading README/docs/AGENTS at 16:55:37. README has no install section, so I used the brief's commands: `py -3.12 -m venv venv` (9 s) and `pip install -e <repo>[dev]` (82 s, clean). `python tasks.py run` from the repo root worked first time in 9.6 s and matched the README narrative (best -5.37031, 11 of 20 rejected). `init my-problem/` wrote only evolvekit.yaml + .env.example; running it as-is failed cleanly on the missing skeleton, then (after I wrote a skeleton) ABORTed on required_functions with exit 0, then failed with a bare "stage proxy: exit code 2" (evaluate.py missing; stderr only in runs.jsonl), then preflight went "clean" while the score objective still named a KPI my evaluator never emits (all scores -0), then the run crashed with a raw traceback because fake_responses.yaml does not exist. param_lhs-only was impossible (big_step_every: 0 rejected; plateau big step calls the strong model), so I wrote a one-entry fake_responses.yaml; my own problem completed at 17:01:35. Then binpacking preflight/run/status/leaderboard --html into S\runs\bp1: all worked; I served the HTML from a local http.server (my PID, killed afterwards) and inspected it: table + archive grid, but no SVG chart despite the README, spend differs from status, no stop reason, no rejected list, no code. Newcomer mistakes: wrong path, other cwd, typo'd keys and YAML errors are handled very well (exit 2, key paths, line numbers). status on a missing dir exits 0 and creates it. Re-running a finished or budget-stopped run resumes and spends a fresh generations/budget allowance each time ($0.0524 against a $0.01 cap after three invocations). A different problem's config pointed at an existing run dir merges silently. --generations 0 evaluates the seed only. A true Ctrl+C could not be delivered in this TTY-less harness (verified against a sleeping control child), so I used CTRL_BREAK on my own PID: redirected log was 0 bytes (stdout is block-buffered), the stale lock was reclaimed and the run resumed. Circlepacking example matched the README (2.57023 in 2.7 s). All processes I started have exited; runs\demo was restored after a bare-interpreter test wiped it.

entries.title: Re-using a run dir silently merges a different (or edited) problem into the ledger; the default run dir is a fixed cwd-relative runs/latest
entries.step: Re-running after changing the config/skeleton (default run dir), and pointing the binpacking config at a run dir created by the circlepacking example
entries.command: cd S\bp-copy (a copy of examples/binpacking); V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir S\runs\circles-mixed --generations 1   (circles-mixed = copy of a finished circlepacking run). Earlier, organically: cd S\my-problem; V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml  twice, fixing required_functions in between.
entries.observed:
resumed 6 candidate(s) from runs.jsonl (2/16 cells occupied (complexity[4] x mean_openness[4]))
gen 3  3 child(ren)  best=2.57023 ...
| 1 | g001-c0002 | 1 | 2.57023 | ... (circle-packing candidate)
| 6 | g003-c0009 | 3 | -5.61986 | ... lineage g001-c0002 < g000-c0001 (bin-packing child bred from a circle-packing parent)
seed score  : 2.54142
best score  : 2.57023
exit=0. No warning. In my own scaffold flow the first failed seed stayed in runs\latest after I fixed the config: '2 candidate(s) logged, 1 rejected'.
entries.expected: A run dir remembers a fingerprint of the config/skeleton/evaluator that created it. On mismatch: refuse (exit non-zero) with 'this run dir was created by <config> with a different problem; use a new --run-dir or --fresh'. At minimum a loud warning when skeleton hash or score definition differs.
entries.why_it_matters: A newcomer iterates on skeleton/evaluator/score and re-runs the same command; because the default run dir is always <cwd>/runs/latest, every re-run resumes stale candidates scored under the old evaluator. The leaderboard then mixes incomparable scores and parents, and nothing says so. This is a silent wrong result reachable with pure defaults.
entries.suggested_fix: Write a run manifest (config path + hash of skeleton, stages, score) into the run dir at creation; compare on resume and refuse or require --force-resume. Consider a timestamped default run dir (runs/<config-stem>-<timestamp>) with runs/latest as a pointer, and print 'resuming existing run' far more prominently.

entries.title: budget.max_usd and search.generations are per invocation, not per run dir: re-running the same command spends the 'hard cap' again
entries.step: Reusing a finished run dir / re-running the same command after a budget stop
entries.command: cd S\bp-copy; lowbudget.yaml = 'extends: evolvekit.yaml' + 'budget: {max_usd: 0.01}'; V -m evolvekit run --config lowbudget.yaml --run-dir runs/budget   (run three times). Also: V -m evolvekit run --config examples/binpacking/evolvekit.yaml --run-dir S\runs\bp1-reuse on a finished 6-generation run.
entries.observed:
1st: stop reason : budget.max_usd reached: $0.0155 of $0.0100 / spend : $0.0155 over 15 call(s)
2nd: resumed 11 candidate(s)... gen 5 ... spent=$0.0025 ... stop reason : budget.max_usd reached: $0.0184 of $0.0100 / spend : $0.0339 over 36 call(s)
3rd: stop reason : budget.max_usd reached: $0.0185 of $0.0100 / spend : $0.0524 over 57 call(s)
Finished run re-run: 'resumed 20 candidate(s)', then gen 7..12 ran, spend $0.0218 -> $0.0997, 'stop reason : generations exhausted' again. The per-generation 'spent=' restarts from 0 on resume while the next line 'economics cum=' is cumulative (gen 7: spent=$0.0022 vs cum=$0.0239). Each invocation also overshoots the cap by 55-85%.
entries.expected: README calls it 'a hard cost budget' and says the ledger 'resumes cleanly'. I expected the cap and the generation count to apply to the run directory: a finished run says 'already complete (6/6 generations); pass --generations N to extend', and a budget-stopped run refuses to continue until max_usd is raised.
entries.why_it_matters: With a paid provider, pressing up-arrow + Enter on a finished or budget-stopped run silently buys another full allowance. The two spend figures printed on adjacent lines disagree, so the user cannot tell which one the guard reads.
entries.suggested_fix: Enforce budget.max_usd / max_tokens against the cumulative usage.jsonl total; treat search.generations as a run total (or document loudly that it is 'N more per invocation' and add --extend). Make 'spent=' cumulative or label it 'this session'. Document the possible overshoot (one generation / one big step).

entries.title: Objective/weight/penalty KPI that the evaluator never emits is silently scored as 0; preflight reports 'clean'
entries.step: Running the init scaffold with my own evaluator (emits 'loss') while the scaffold's score block still says objective: excess_pct; then a deliberate typo 'losss' in both objective and weights
entries.command: cd S\my-problem; V -m evolvekit preflight --config typo6.yaml ; V -m evolvekit run --config typo6.yaml --run-dir runs/typo6 --generations 3
entries.observed:
preflight: stage proxy ok  kpis: a=0, b=0, loss=10 ... no mention of the missing objective KPI, no seed score printed; with the unmodified scaffold: 'verdict : clean (0 failure(s), 0 warning(s))' exit=0.
run: gen table 'best -0' for every generation; 'seed score : -0 / best score : -0 / improvement : 0 / stop reason : generations exhausted' exit=0.
entries.expected: Preflight (whose job is 'fix the harness before spending') fails: 'evaluate.score.objective "excess_pct" was not emitted by stage proxy/full; emitted KPIs: a, b, loss'. Same for weights and penalties KPIs. Preflight should also print the seed's computed score so I can sanity-check it.
entries.why_it_matters: The init scaffold ships objective: excess_pct and penalty priority_errors, so every newcomer who writes their own evaluator starts in this state. A paid run would burn its whole budget optimising a constant.
entries.suggested_fix: In preflight and at gen 0 of run, verify that objective, every weights key, every penalties kpi and every archive descriptor kpi appear in the seed's emitted KPIs; treat a missing objective as a failure (exit 2 / ABORT). Print 'seed score = ...' in preflight.

entries.title: init scaffold cannot be run as its own 'Next:' message says: it references three files it never writes
entries.step: init into scratch dir and run the scaffold as-is following the printed next steps
entries.command: V -m evolvekit init my-problem/ ; cd my-problem ; V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml
entries.observed:
wrote ...\evolvekit.yaml / wrote ...\.env.example
Next: point problem.skeleton at your skeleton file, then
  python -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml
-> config error: problem.skeleton: no such file: ...\my-problem\skeleton.py (exit=2). After adding a skeleton I still hit, one failure at a time: required_functions: [priority] (bin-packing specific), missing evaluate.py, score objective excess_pct / penalty priority_errors (bin-packing specific), missing fake_responses.yaml (raw traceback). Five edit-run cycles before anything ran.
entries.expected: init writes a minimal runnable toy: skeleton.py with an EVOLVE-BLOCK, evaluate.py emitting the KPI the config scores, and a fake_responses.yaml, so 'init; preflight; run' succeeds offline and I then replace the pieces. Or at least the Next message lists all files I must create.
entries.why_it_matters: The scaffold is the documented step 0; as shipped it is a bin-packing config with the bin-packing files removed. docs/new-experiment.md quietly admits copying an example 'is usually faster', which is the real path.
entries.suggested_fix: Have init emit skeleton.py, evaluate.py and fake_responses.yaml stubs (a 10-line toy), or add `init --from binpacking`. Make the Next message enumerate every referenced-but-missing file and suggest `preflight` first.

entries.title: Evaluator stderr is hidden: run and preflight print only 'exit code 2'
entries.step: Running / preflighting the scaffold when evaluate.py did not exist yet (same would apply to any evaluator crash)
entries.command: cd S\my-problem; V -m evolvekit preflight --config evolvekit.yaml ; V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml
entries.observed:
preflight: 'stage proxy  FAILED  0.1s' / '    failure : exit code 2' / 'FAILURE : stage proxy: exit code 2' / 'verdict : failures' exit=2.
run: 'ABORT: seed failed evaluation - fix the harness before spending: stage proxy: exit code 2'.
The actual cause was only in runs.jsonl -> last_failure: "stage proxy: exit code 2\npython: can't open file '...\\my-problem\\evaluate.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory". Preflight uses a temp dir and no run dir, so there the stderr is not recoverable at all.
entries.expected: The failing command line and the last ~20 lines of its stderr printed under the FAILED stage, in both preflight and run.
entries.why_it_matters: Preflight is the documented tool for debugging a new harness, and an evaluator traceback is the most common thing a newcomer needs to see. 'exit code 2' forces me to reconstruct and run the command by hand without knowing the candidate path.
entries.suggested_fix: Print the expanded command and the stderr tail for any failed command stage (the data is already captured in last_failure). In preflight add --keep-tmp or print the temp paths.

entries.title: README promises an inline-SVG best-score-vs-USD chart in the HTML dashboard; the generated HTML contains no SVG
entries.step: leaderboard --html on the binpacking run, then opening the HTML to judge whether it tells me what happened
entries.command: V -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir S\runs\bp1 --html S\board.html ; grep -c "<svg" S\board.html (also for runs/demo and my own run)
entries.observed: wrote ...\board.html (41891 bytes). grep -c '<svg' -> 0 for all three runs. DOM check in the browser: headings = ['evolvekit leaderboard','Archive grid'], svgs: 0. The stylesheet contains .chart/.line/.dot rules but no chart element is emitted. The HTML also has no economics table (the markdown output has one).
entries.expected: README 'Economics': 'a dependency-free inline-SVG chart of best score against cumulative USD in the HTML dashboard (one dot per generation ...)'. I expected to see the run's trajectory.
entries.why_it_matters: The HTML is the artefact a newcomer opens to understand the run; the one view that shows progress over time/spend is documented but absent, so the page is a static ranking only.
entries.suggested_fix: Wire the economics series into the HTML writer used by the CLI (chart + the per-generation table), and add a test asserting '<svg' is present when usage.jsonl has rows.

entries.title: Progress output is block-buffered when stdout is redirected: log stays 0 bytes until exit and is lost on kill
entries.step: Interrupting a run whose output was redirected to a log file; then polling a redirected run
entries.command: cd S\bp-copy; V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir runs/tail1 > S\tail1.log 2>&1 &  then poll `stat -c %s tail1.log` and `wc -l runs/tail1/runs.jsonl` each second
entries.observed: t=1s log_bytes=0 runs_rows=1 / t=2s log_bytes=0 runs_rows=4 / t=3s log_bytes=0 runs_rows=7 / t=4s log_bytes=0 runs_rows=10 / t=5s log_bytes=5505 runs_rows=20 (process exited). The run I interrupted at 3 s left a 0-byte int2.log although generation 1 had completed.
entries.expected: Each 'gen N ...' line appears in the log as it happens (flush per line), so `tail -f run.log` works and a crash leaves the history plus the stop reason.
entries.why_it_matters: The README targets hour-long evaluators; anyone running `... > run.log` or under nohup sees nothing for hours and cannot tell a hang from progress. Because the stop reason is only ever printed to stdout, a killed run loses it entirely.
entries.suggested_fix: print(..., flush=True) for progress lines or sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True) in the CLI; additionally append progress and the final stop reason to <run_dir>/run.log.

entries.title: status cannot tell a live run from a dead or finished one, and the stop reason is not stored anywhere
entries.step: status during a run, after an interrupt, and after completion
entries.command: V -m evolvekit status --run-dir runs/lock1 (while pid 10484 held the lock) ; V -m evolvekit status --run-dir runs/int2 (after I killed the run) ; V -m evolvekit status --run-dir S\runs\bp1 (finished) ; grep -rl "generations exhausted\|stop_reason" S\runs\bp1
entries.observed: All three print the same shape: 'candidates : 4 (1 rejected) ... generations : 1 / archive : no archive.json snapshot yet / best : ... / llm calls / tokens / spend'. No 'running (pid N since ...)', no 'interrupted / stale lock', no stop reason, no budget cap or remaining, no planned generations, no timestamps or elapsed time. grep for the stop reason in the run dir: no matches.
entries.expected: A first line such as 'state: RUNNING pid 10484 since 15:10:01, gen 2 of 6' / 'STOPPED: generations exhausted at 15:02:32' / 'DEAD: stale lock from pid 11080', plus 'spend $0.0218 of $1.00 cap'.
entries.why_it_matters: 'Is it still going, and if not why did it stop?' is the first question after walking away from a run; the .lock file has the data but status ignores it. Felt minor on 6-second runs, would be major on hour-long ones.
entries.suggested_fix: Have status read .lock (pid liveness, start time) and a persisted summary.json (stop reason, end time, generations run/planned), and print spend against budget caps.

entries.title: Rejected total does not equal its own breakdown; static hard rejects and unparseable responses are invisible in console, status and HTML
entries.step: Reading the quickstart output and trying to account for every rejection
entries.command: python tasks.py run ; V -m evolvekit status --run-dir S\runs\bp1 ; then a Python one-liner printing id + reject_reason from runs.jsonl
entries.observed: '20 candidate(s) logged, 11 rejected (1 no-op, 6 duplicate, 2 behavioural)' and 'rejected : 11 (1 no-op, 6 duplicate, 2 behavioural)' -> 1+6+2 = 9. status: 'candidates : 20 (11 rejected)'. The missing two exist only in runs.jsonl: 'g004-c0012 | forbidden import(s): ['os']' and 'g004-c0013 | could not apply response: response contained neither a SEARCH/REPLACE block nor a code fence'. Neither produced a console line during gen 4. In my own run: '2 rejected (0 no-op, 0 duplicate, 0 behavioural)'. The HTML lists no rejected candidate at all (grep for g001-c0003, g002-c0006, g003-c0008 -> 0).
entries.expected: Breakdown sums to the total, e.g. '11 rejected (1 no-op, 6 duplicate, 2 behavioural, 1 static, 1 unapplied)', a console line per reject like the other verdicts, and a collapsed 'Rejected' table in the HTML with reasons.
entries.why_it_matters: The README says stage 0 is 'the only hard reject' and that ~40% wasted calls is the number to drive down; the two most actionable reject kinds (model emitted garbage / forbidden code) are the ones hidden. With a real model, 'could not apply response' can be the dominant failure.
entries.suggested_fix: Add static/unapplied (and provider-error) buckets to every summary line, log them per child, and include rejected rows with reject_reason in both leaderboards.

entries.title: A missing fake responses file is a raw Python traceback mid-run; preflight does not check it
entries.step: Running the scaffold after skeleton and evaluator existed but fake_responses.yaml did not
entries.command: cd S\my-problem; V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir runs/mismatch   (preflight on the same config had just said 'verdict : clean')
entries.observed:
Traceback (most recent call last): ... File "...\evolvekit\providers\fake.py", line 179, in _load_responses
    raise ProviderError(f"fake provider: responses_path not found: {resolved}")
evolvekit.providers.base.ProviderError: fake provider: responses_path not found: ...\my-problem\fake_responses.yaml
exit=1, printed after 'gen 0 seed score=-0'. With param_lhs-only operators it crashed later, at the first plateau big step (gen 3).
entries.expected: 'config error: models.small.options.responses_path: no such file: ...' at load time (exit 2), like problem.skeleton gets, and preflight catching it without --provider-check since it costs nothing.
entries.why_it_matters: Every other config mistake I made got a one-line key-path error, so this traceback looks like a framework bug; and it fires after the seed has been evaluated and a run dir created.
entries.suggested_fix: Validate responses_path existence in load_config; catch ProviderError in the CLI and print it as 'provider error: ...' with a non-zero exit and a stop reason in the summary.

entries.title: Seed ABORT exits with code 0
entries.step: Running the scaffold whose seed failed evaluation
entries.command: cd S\my-problem; V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml ; echo exit=$?
entries.observed:
gen 0  seed        score=-1000
ABORT: seed failed evaluation - fix the harness before spending: missing required top-level function(s): ['priority']; the module defines ['solve']
... stop reason : seed failed evaluation ...
exit=0
entries.expected: A non-zero exit code for ABORT (preflight documents 0/1/2 and the lock refusal exits 3, so the convention exists).
entries.why_it_matters: Any wrapper script, CI job or `run && leaderboard` chain treats a run that never started as success. The message text itself is excellent.
entries.suggested_fix: Return a distinct non-zero exit code when the stop reason is a seed failure or a provider-error halt; document run's exit codes in README and --help.

entries.title: HTML 'SPENT' ($0.0214) disagrees with status and run summary ($0.0218) for the same run
entries.step: Comparing the HTML dashboard with status for S\runs\bp1
entries.command: V -m evolvekit status --run-dir S\runs\bp1 ; V -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir S\runs\bp1 --html S\board.html ; summed usd in usage.jsonl and in runs.jsonl
entries.observed: status: 'spend : $0.0218'; run summary: 'spend : $0.0218 over 30 call(s)'; HTML tile: '$0.0214 SPENT'. usage.jsonl sum = 0.021772 (includes scratchpad 0.000343); runs.jsonl per-candidate usd sum = 0.02143.
entries.expected: One spend number everywhere, the ledger total, with framework/meta calls shown as their own line if needed.
entries.why_it_matters: Spend is the headline claim of the tool; two official views disagreeing on the first number I compared makes me distrust both, and the gap grows with scratchpad refreshes and embedding calls on real runs.
entries.suggested_fix: Compute the HTML total from usage.jsonl (same function status uses) and show 'of which meta calls: $X'.

entries.title: Leaderboard 'cell' column is stale relative to the archive grid on the same page
entries.step: Reading the HTML for the binpacking run
entries.command: V -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir S\runs\bp1 --html S\board.html (page text read in the browser)
entries.observed: Table: g002-c0005 cell '3,0', g001-c0004 cell '3,1', g001-c0002 cell '3,3'. Archive grid on the same page: g002-c0005 and g001-c0004 sit in row 'complexity 2', g001-c0002 in row 'complexity 0'. Only g004-c0014 (3,2) agrees. Grid axes are labelled with bin indices ('mean_openness 0..3'), not value ranges.
entries.expected: The table shows the candidate's current cell (or labels the column 'cell at insert'), and grid headers show the bin's value range, e.g. 'mean_openness 0.06-0.12'.
entries.why_it_matters: README explains that range: auto re-bins, but a newcomer cross-referencing table and grid concludes one of them is wrong, and cannot map a bin index back to a KPI value.
entries.suggested_fix: Recompute cells from the current archive axes when rendering; print bin edges in grid headers and in status.

entries.title: status / leaderboard on a nonexistent run dir exit 0 and create the directory
entries.step: status on a directory that has no run (typo'd path)
entries.command: V -m evolvekit status --run-dir S\nope ; echo exit=$? ; find S\nope ; V -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir S\emptydir --html S\empty.html
entries.observed:
no runs recorded in ...\quickstart\nope
exit=0
find: .../nope and .../nope/traces now exist. `status` with no arguments likewise created <cwd>\runs\latest\traces. leaderboard on an empty dir: 'No scored candidates yet.' + 'wrote ...\empty.html', exit=0.
entries.expected: 'error: run directory does not exist: ...' (or 'no runs.jsonl in ...'), non-zero exit, and no filesystem side effects from read-only commands.
entries.why_it_matters: A typo in --run-dir looks like 'my run recorded nothing', and litters empty run dirs that later make a real `run` print nothing unusual. Exit 0 defeats scripting.
entries.suggested_fix: Open the ledger read-only in status/leaderboard; do not mkdir; exit 2 when the dir or runs.jsonl is missing.

entries.title: No install instructions; literal Quickstart on a clean interpreter fails, and tasks.py deletes runs/demo before failing
entries.step: Following the README Quickstart exactly as written from a fresh clone
entries.command: py -3.12 -m venv S\venv-bare ; cd <repo> ; S\venv-bare\Scripts\python.exe tasks.py run   (grep of README for 'pip install|venv' finds only `pip install 'evolvekit[entra]'`)
entries.observed:
File "...\evolvekit\config.py", line 15, in <module>
    import yaml
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'
exit=1. Afterwards `ls runs/demo` -> No such file or directory: the previous demo results had been wiped before the failure (I restored them by re-running with the installed venv).
entries.expected: A three-line Install block above Quickstart (python -m venv .venv; pip install -e .[dev]; Python >= 3.11), and tasks.py removing the old demo dir only once the new run has started (or saying 'removing runs/demo').
entries.why_it_matters: It is the very first command in the README. A Python developer recovers in a minute or two, but the [dev] extra, the minimum Python version and the editable install are all guesswork from pyproject.toml. With the install done, pip took 82 s and the quickstart 9.6 s, which is good.
entries.suggested_fix: Add an Install section; have tasks.py check imports and print 'run pip install -e .[dev] first'; make `python tasks.py --help` print usage instead of KeyError: '--help'.

entries.title: Default --run-dir (cwd\runs\latest) and --config are undocumented; README command list implies `run` writes runs/demo; most flags have no help text
entries.step: Reading --help for every subcommand, then following the README command block in order
entries.command: V -m evolvekit run --help ; V -m evolvekit status --help ; cd S\elsewhere ; V -m evolvekit run --config ../my-problem/evolvekit.yaml --generations 1
entries.observed: run --help lists '--config CONFIG  --run-dir RUN_DIR  --generations GENERATIONS  --quiet' with no descriptions or defaults. The run landed in 'run dir : ...\elsewhere\runs\latest' (cwd-relative, while skeleton/evaluator paths are config-relative). README block: `run --config examples/binpacking/evolvekit.yaml` is followed by `status --run-dir runs/demo`, but only `tasks.py run` writes runs/demo. `preflight --candidate` help says 'as saved under a run's candidates/ directory' - the real location is <run_dir>\work\candidates\, and work/ is absent from README's run-dir inventory.
entries.expected: argparse help strings with defaults ('--run-dir DIR  default: ./runs/latest, resumes if it exists'), and README commands that chain (same --run-dir throughout).
entries.why_it_matters: Combined with silent resume, not knowing that every un-flagged run shares ./runs/latest is how a newcomer ends up with a mixed ledger.
entries.suggested_fix: Fill in help= and defaults for every flag, fix the README sequence to pass --run-dir consistently, document work/candidates and work/stage_out.

entries.title: No documented way to get the winning program out of a run
entries.step: Understanding the outputs: 'what is the best program the run found?'
entries.command: V -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir S\runs\bp1 --html S\board.html ; V -m evolvekit leaderboard --help ; ls S\runs\bp1\work\candidates
entries.observed: Leaderboards (markdown and HTML) show ids, scores, lineage, tokens - no code, no diff, no link. No show/export subcommand ('{init,preflight,run,status,leaderboard}'). I found the source by browsing: runs.jsonl rows have a 'block' field and work\candidates\g004-c0014.py holds the spliced module; neither is described as 'the result' in README or docs/new-experiment.md.
entries.expected: The end-of-run summary prints 'best candidate: g004-c0014 -> <path to .py>', and/or `evolvekit show <id>` / `export --best out.py`; the HTML row expands to the block and its diff against the parent.
entries.why_it_matters: The evolved block is the product of the whole exercise; after a successful run the docs leave me holding an id.
entries.suggested_fix: Add `evolvekit show/export`, print the best candidate's file path in the summary and status, embed collapsible code + parent diff in the HTML.

entries.title: A zero-LLM param_lhs-only search is not possible: big steps cannot be disabled
entries.step: Making my own problem run without any provider, using only the free param_lhs operator
entries.command: cd S\my-problem; set search.operators: {param_lhs: 1.0}, then big_step_every: 0, then big_step_every: 1000 ; V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir runs/own2
entries.observed: big_step_every: 0 -> 'config error: search.big_step_every: must be >= 1, got 0'. big_step_every: 1000 -> gens 1-2 ran on param_lhs, then at the gen-3 plateau the run built the strong provider and crashed (ProviderError: fake provider: responses_path not found ...). I had to hand-write a fake_responses.yaml to finish a run.
entries.expected: big_step_every: 0 (or operators without LLM entries) means 'never call a model'; models section optional in that case. README's operator table sells param_lhs as 'no LLM call' but never says a run still needs a working strong model.
entries.why_it_matters: A keyless newcomer (or someone tuning constants only) cannot use the one operator that needs no provider without faking one; on a paid config it means a constants sweep still spends strong-model money on every plateau.
entries.suggested_fix: Allow big_step_every: 0 and skip plateau big steps when disabled; skip scratchpad/big-step calls when no LLM operator is configured; document it.

entries.title: Evaluator command's `python` is the base interpreter, not the venv running evolvekit - documented only in the pyvrp example README
entries.step: Checking which interpreter runs `python evaluate.py ...` when evolvekit is started from an un-activated venv
entries.command: cd S\whichpy (copy of my problem whose evaluator puts sys.executable into text_feedback); V -m evolvekit preflight --config evolvekit.yaml
entries.observed: | C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\python.exe point=(0.000,0.000) ...   while evolvekit itself ran from S\venv\Scripts\python.exe. examples/pyvrp/README.md lines ~402-412 explain this ('Activating the venv does not help; this was measured'); README 'Adding a problem' and docs/new-experiment.md both show `command: "python evaluate.py ..."` with no caveat.
entries.expected: Either `python` in a stage command is resolved to sys.executable, or a {python} placeholder exists, or the main docs warn about it next to the evaluator contract.
entries.why_it_matters: The first evaluator that imports numpy (installed only in the project venv) fails with 'exit code 1' and, per the stderr entry above, no visible ImportError.
entries.suggested_fix: Add a {python} placeholder that expands to sys.executable and use it in init/examples; move the pyvrp note into README 'Adding a problem'.

entries.title: A hard interrupt discards the in-flight generation's paid calls; candidates appear to be logged per generation
entries.step: Interrupting a run (CTRL_BREAK on my own PID) and re-running the same command
entries.command: V S\interrupt2.py break 3.0 S\int2.log S\int2.pid -- V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir runs/int2 ; wc -l runs/int2/runs.jsonl runs/int2/usage.jsonl ; then the same run command again
entries.observed: After the kill: runs.jsonl 4 rows (seed + generation 1), usage.jsonl 9 rows (generation 2's five calls already billed), status 'llm calls : 9 / spend : $0.0034'. Re-run: 'reclaimed a stale lock from dead pid 11080' / 'resumed 4 candidate(s) from runs.jsonl' and generation 2 was bred again from scratch, then ran through gen 7 (six more, not six total). Final: 'spend : $0.0267 over 42 call(s)' vs $0.0218/30 calls uninterrupted. A true Ctrl+C could not be tested: GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent had no effect even on a sleeping control child in this TTY-less harness.
entries.expected: Each child is appended to runs.jsonl as soon as it is proposed/evaluated so a resume re-uses it; resume prints 'gen 2 was incomplete: N paid call(s) had no recorded candidate'.
entries.why_it_matters: Cheap here, but with hour-long stages an interrupt can throw away a generation of evaluations and their LLM spend without saying so. Lock reclaim and resume themselves worked well.
entries.suggested_fix: Log candidates incrementally (proposed -> evaluated) and reconcile usage.jsonl against runs.jsonl on resume, reporting orphaned spend.

entries.title: Seed line prints the public score while 'best=' prints the hold-out-penalised rank, so the first generation looks like a regression; 'improvement' and 'd best' use different bases
entries.step: Reading the console output of my own problem's run
entries.command: cd S\my-problem; V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir runs/own3
entries.observed:
gen 0  seed        score=-10
gen 1  3 child(ren)  best=-11.45 ...
... economics: gen 3 d best '+10.6'; summary: 'seed score : -10 / best score : -0.5 / best rank : -0.85 / improvement : 9.5'.
entries.expected: The seed line shows both ('score=-10 rank=-11.45'), and improvement is computed on the ranking score everything else uses (or both are shown).
entries.why_it_matters: With any hold-out gap the very first progress line reads as 'best got worse than the seed', and the two improvement figures cannot be reconciled without reading the hold-out section of the README.
entries.suggested_fix: Print rank alongside score on the seed line; label columns 'best rank'; report improvement in rank terms.

entries.title: Em dash in the ABORT/stop-reason message renders as a replacement character in Git Bash
entries.step: Reading the ABORT message in Git Bash on Windows
entries.command: cd S\my-problem; V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml   (Git Bash)
entries.observed: ABORT: seed failed evaluation � fix the harness before spending: ...   and   stop reason : seed failed evaluation � fix the harness ...   In PowerShell with [Console]::OutputEncoding = utf-8 the same line shows a proper em dash.
entries.expected: ASCII punctuation in console messages, or stdout reconfigured to UTF-8.
entries.why_it_matters: Cosmetic, but it is in the single most important error a newcomer sees and makes the tool look broken on Windows.
entries.suggested_fix: Use ' - ' or ': ' in CLI strings, or call sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') at CLI start.

entries.title: End-of-run output is noisy: economics printed twice, --quiet still prints ~35 lines, preflight emits six boilerplate notes on the shipped example; README samples are stale
entries.step: Reading run, run --quiet and preflight output for the shipped binpacking example
entries.command: python tasks.py run ; V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir runs/quiet --generations 2 --quiet ; V -m evolvekit preflight --config examples/binpacking/evolvekit.yaml
entries.observed: Every run ends with the markdown '### Economics' table immediately followed by the same data as a fixed-width table. --quiet removed only the per-generation lines. Preflight on the shipped config printed six notes ('timeout 120s is 1003x the seed's 0.12s...', 'timeout 120s is at or above 60s. If this evaluator is wall-clock bounded...') where the README sample shows one. README sample numbers differ from actual output (README gen 1 '0.0011 ... $0.0044/unit', gen 3 'spent=$0.0036'; actual '0.0016 ... $0.0062/unit', 'spent=$0.0051').
entries.expected: One economics table; --quiet prints only the final summary block; preflight collapses repeated notes ('3 stages have timeouts >1000x the seed'); README samples regenerated from the current demo.
entries.why_it_matters: The useful lines (stop reason, best, run dir) scroll under two copies of the same table, and a wall of notes on the vendor's own example teaches newcomers to ignore preflight notes.
entries.suggested_fix: Drop the duplicate table (or put markdown behind a flag), make --quiet quiet, dedupe notes per kind, regenerate README snippets in CI.

entries.title: --generations accepts negative values silently; --generations 0 (seed-only) is undocumented
entries.step: Passing --generations 0 and -1
entries.command: V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir runs/gen0 --generations 0 ; V -m evolvekit run --config evolvekit.yaml --run-dir runs/genneg --generations -1
entries.observed: Both: seed evaluated, 'stop reason : generations exhausted', 'spend : $0.0000 over 0 call(s)', a run dir with runs.jsonl/archive.json created, exit=0. ('--generations two' is correctly rejected by argparse, exit 2.)
entries.expected: 0 documented as 'evaluate the seed only' (it is a handy smoke test) and negative values rejected like search.big_step_every: 0 is.
entries.why_it_matters: Harmless, but inconsistent with the otherwise strict config validation, and the seed-only behaviour is useful enough to advertise.
entries.suggested_fix: Validate --generations >= 0 and describe 0 in the flag's help text.

unanswered_questions: Is this run alive, finished, crashed or interrupted right now? status prints the same fields in all four cases and ignores .lock.
Why did a run stop? The stop reason is printed once to stdout and is not stored in any file in the run dir (grep found nothing), so it is lost with the terminal or a buffered log.
How much budget is left (USD, tokens, full evals per day) and how many generations remain of the planned total? status shows spend but no caps, and generations/budget turned out to be per invocation.
Which spend figure is the truth: status/run ($0.0218) or the HTML tile ($0.0214)? And which one does the budget guard read - the per-session 'spent=' or the cumulative 'economics cum='?

What were the 2 of 11 rejections that the breakdown '(1 no-op, 6 duplicate, 2 behavioural)' does not account for? Only a manual read of runs.jsonl answered it (forbidden import, unparseable response).
What is the winning program's source and what changed versus its parent? No CLI or HTML view shows code; I found work\candidates\<id>.py and the runs.jsonl 'block' field by browsing.
What KPI value ranges do archive bins 0..3 correspond to after range: auto re-binning, and why does the leaderboard's cell differ from the grid's?
What does a real Ctrl+C do (graceful stop with summary, or immediate death)? I could not deliver one in this TTY-less harness; docs only say interrupted runs 'resume cleanly'.
After an interrupt, how many paid LLM calls had no recorded candidate (orphaned spend)? usage.jsonl had 9 rows vs 4 candidates but no tool reports the difference.
How long did the run / each generation / each stage take, and what is the ETA? No elapsed time or timestamps in run output, status or HTML (only created_at inside runs.jsonl).
Does a run dir belong to the config I am about to run against it? Nothing records or checks which config, skeleton or evaluator produced a ledger.
What are run's exit codes? preflight documents 0/1/2 and the lock refusal is 3, but ABORT, budget stop and patience stop all returned 0.
Is there any supported way to run with no LLM at all (param_lhs only)? big_step_every: 0 is rejected and plateau big steps always call the strong model.
went_well: pip install -e .[dev] into a fresh py -3.12 venv worked first time (82 s, no build problems on Windows).
`python tasks.py run` worked first time in 9.6 s and its numbers matched the README narrative exactly (seed -5.871 -> -5.61986 -> -5.37031, 11 of 20 rejected, 5 cells, breadth 3->4->3).

Config validation is excellent: unknown keys list the known keys with a key path ('search: unknown key(s) ['childrn_per_generation']; known keys are [...]'), bad enum/number values name the path and the offending value, objective/weights mismatch is caught, all exit 2 before any run dir is created.
YAML syntax errors report the file, line and column; empty file and non-mapping root get their own clear messages.
Wrong --config path and wrong cwd give 'config error: config file not found: <absolute path>' with exit 2 and no side effects.
Config-relative resolution works: running from an unrelated cwd with a relative --config path still found skeleton.py and ran evaluate.py correctly.
The seed-failure ABORT text is genuinely helpful: 'missing required top-level function(s): ['priority']; the module defines ['solve']'.

Run lock: a concurrent second run is refused with exit 3 and a message naming the pid, start time and the .lock path; a lock left by a killed process was reclaimed automatically ('reclaimed a stale lock from dead pid 11080') and the run resumed from runs.jsonl.
init refuses to overwrite existing files without --force.
preflight output for a working harness is informative: per-stage KPIs, evaluator notes, durations, hold-out included, plus a projected wall clock; exit codes 0/1/2 behaved as documented.
param_lhs worked on my own problem with just a '# PARAMS:' line, at zero cost.
The examples' fake_responses.yaml header documents the fake provider's format well enough to write my own without reading source.
The circlepacking example matched the README exactly (2.54142 -> 2.57023, 2.7 s).
The HTML is a single self-contained file, renders cleanly, and its footer explains rank vs score and the '!' flag; the archive grid with 'N tried, M children' per cell is a nice view.
I never had to read evolvekit/*.py or tests/ to make progress.
